title: Read the PIN out of a clear PIN block

blocks.text: The certification lab runs a test issuer. Its software security module decrypts each field 52 and passes the clear block, with the card number of the message, to `PinBlockReader.pin`, which returns the PIN the cardholder typed. The issuer then compares that PIN with the test card's own.

The lab's devices are a mix: the older PIN pads send ISO format 0, the new ones format 3, and one ATM vendor's test machine sends format 1, often without knowing the card number. Nothing else is in use, and a block in any other format is refused.

A reader that gets a block wrong does one of two things, and both cost certification time. It returns a PIN where it should have refused the block, so a wrong PIN can be approved; or it refuses a PIN the cardholder typed right, and the vendor goes hunting for a bug in a pad that works.
Finish the two methods marked `TODO` in `src/main/java/com/example/practice/PinBlockReader.java`:

items: `pinField(block, pan)`: the PIN field the device built, before it mixed anything in;
`pinFrom(field)`: the PIN in it, or an `IllegalArgumentException` when the field isn't one a device would build.

blocks.text: `pin` already checks that the block is 16 hex digits and calls the two. About twenty lines in total. `org.jpos.iso.ISOUtil` has `hex2byte`, `xor`, `hexString` and `isNumeric` if you want them.

cases.says: the PIN typed on a format 0 device is read back from the clear block and the card number
a block in a format the lab's devices don't send, or with a card number its format can't use, is refused
the card number contributes the 12 digits before its check digit, which matters on a card whose last digits differ
the PIN length is one hexadecimal digit, so PINs of ten to twelve digits are read too
a block read with another card's number is refused because its fill is wrong, even when the digits look like a PIN
format 3 is read like format 0 but its fill is any of A to F
format 1 carries no card number, so nothing is XORed out of it

origin.section: 8.3. Format 0 Gives the Same Block Every Time, So Format 3 Adds Random Fill

concepts: Format 0 fills with F and gives the same block every time; format 3 fills with random A to F, and format 1 fills randomly and leaves the card number out, so the reader must act on the format digit.
A format 0 PIN block is the PIN field XOR 0000 and the 12 card-number digits before the check digit, so it can be read only with the card number it was built for.
